I've been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for thirty years now, and at my age I don't go looking for big changes. Most of my land — about 6.5 mu — I'll keep in the wheat-maize double crop because that's my insurance: the wheat gives us enough flour for the year and a bit of cash, and the maize covers school fees and input costs for the next season. The extension fellow keeps talking about cutting back nitrogen, but I remember two years ago when my neighbor Liu cut too much and his wheat went yellow at jointing — lost nearly a hundred jin per mu. I figure 18 kg of N per mu for wheat is about right; maybe a touch more than they recommend, but I'd rather waste a little money than face a bad harvest. I'll put base fertilizer down before planting with the rotary tiller, then topdress at green-up. For the summer maize, there's no time for tillage after the wheat comes off in early June — it's got to be no-till planting straight into the stubble, hybrid seed of course, everyone uses hybrid now. I'll irrigate the wheat four times — winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling — and the maize twice if the rains don't come. I also keep 1.5 mu in cotton because my wife's sister's family did well with cotton prices last autumn, and that extra cash is useful. Cotton means more pest sprays though — I'll need four applications for bollworm — and rotary tillage in April. I'll manage the phosphorus and potassium alongside the nitrogen, nothing fancy, just compound fertilizer from the co-op.
